[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (2) The written evidence must –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (a) identify the grounds on which the judgment was obtained;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (b) state whether the defendant objected to the jurisdiction and, if he did, the grounds of his objection;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (c) show that the judgment –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (i) has been served in accordance with Part 6 and rule 40.4, and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (ii) is not subject to a stay of execution;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (d) state –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (i) the date on which the time for appealing expired or will expire;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (ii) whether an appeal notice has been filed;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (iii) the status of any application for permission to appeal; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (iv) whether an appeal is pending;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (e) state whether the judgment provides for the payment of a sum of money, and if so, the amount in respect of which it remains unsatisfied;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (f) state whether interest is recoverable on the judgment, and if so, either –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (i) the amount of interest which has accrued up to the date of the application, or

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (ii) the rate of interest, the date from which it is recoverable, and the date on which it ceases to accrue. ## III ENFORCEMENT OF UNITED KINGDOM JUDGMENTS IN OTHER PARTS OF THE UNITED KINGDOM

## Interpretation

## 74.14

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.14] In this Section –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.14] (a) ‘money provision’ means a provision for the payment of one or more sums of money in a judgment whose enforcement is governed by section 18 of, and Schedule 6 to, the 1982 Act; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.14] (b) ‘non-money provision’ means a provision for any relief or remedy not requiring payment of a sum of money in a judgment whose enforcement is governed by section 18 of, and Schedule 7 to, the 1982 Act. ## Registration of money judgments in the High Court

## 74.15

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.15] (1) This rule applies to applications to the High Court under paragraph 5 of Schedule 6 to the 1982 Act for the registration of a certificate for the enforcement of the money provisions of a judgment –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.15] (a) which has been given by a court in another part of the United Kingdom, and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.15] (b) to which section 18 of that Act applies. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.15] (2) The certificate must within six months of the date of its issue be filed in the Central Office of the Senior Courts, together with a copy certified by written evidence to be a true copy. ## Registration of non-money judgments in the High Court

## 74.16

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.16] (1) This rule applies to applications to the High Court under paragraph 5 of Schedule 7 to the 1982 Act for the registration for enforcement of the non-money provisions of a judgment –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.16] (a) which has been given by a court in another part of the United Kingdom, and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.16] (b) to which section 18 of that Act applies. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.16] (2) An application under paragraph (1) may be made without notice. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.16] (3) An application under paragraph (1) must be accompanied

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.16] (a) by a certified copy of the judgment issued under Schedule 7 to the 1982 Act; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.16] (b) by a certificate, issued not more than six months before the date of the application, stating that the conditions set out in paragraph 3 of Schedule 7 are satisfied in relation to the judgment. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.16] (4) Rule 74.6 applies to judgments registered under Schedule 7 to the 1982 Act as it applies to judgments registered under section 4 of that Act. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.16] (5) Rule 74.7 applies to applications to set aside the registration of a judgment under paragraph 9 of Schedule 7 to the 1982 Act as it applies to applications to set aside registrations under the 1920 and 1933 Acts. ## Certificates of High Court and County Court money judgments

## 74.17

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.17] (1) This rule applies to applications under paragraph 2 of Schedule 6 to the 1982 Act for a certificate to enable the money provisions of a judgment of the High Court or of the County Court to be enforced in another part of the United Kingdom. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.17] (2) The judgment creditor may apply for a certificate by filing at the court where the judgment was given or has been entered written evidence stating –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.17] (a) the name and address of the judgment creditor and, if known, of the judgment debtor;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.17] (b) the sums payable and unsatisfied under the money provisions of the judgment;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.17] (c) where interest is recoverable on the judgment, either –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.17] (i) the amount of interest which has accrued up to the date of the application, or

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.17] (ii) the rate of interest, the date from which it is recoverable, and the date on which it ceases to accrue;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.17] (d) that the judgment is not stayed;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.17] (e) the date on which the time for appealing expired or will expire;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.17] (f) whether an appeal notice has been filed;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.17] (g) the status of any application for permission to appeal; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.17] (h) whether an appeal is pending. ## Certified copies of High Court and County Court non-money judgments

## 74.18

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.18] (1) This rule applies to applications under paragraph 2 of Schedule 7 to the 1982 Act for a certified copy of a judgment of the High Court or of the County Court to which section 18 of the Act applies and which contains non-money provisions for enforcement in another part of the United Kingdom. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.18] (2) An application under paragraph (1) may be made without notice. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.18] (3) The applicant may apply for a certified copy of a judgment by filing at the court where the judgment was given or has been entered written evidence stating –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.18] (a) full particulars of the judgment;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.18] (b) the name and address of the judgment creditor and, if known, of the judgment debtor;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.18] (c) that the judgment is not stayed;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.18] (d) the date on which the time for appealing expired or will expire;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.18] (e) whether an appeal notice has been filed;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.18] (f) the status of any application for permission to appeal; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.18] (g) whether an appeal is pending. ## VI RECOGNITION AND ENFORCEMENT OF PROTECTION MEASURES

## Interpretation

## 74.34 In this Section—

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.34 In this Section—] (a) Omitted

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.34 In this Section—] (b) Omitted

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.34 In this Section—] (c) “Article 11 notice” means the notification required by Article 11 of the Protection Measures Regulation;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.34 In this Section—] (d) Omitted

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.34 In this Section—] (e) “incoming protection measure” means a protection measure that has been ordered in a Member State of the European Union other than the United Kingdom or Denmark;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.34 In this Section—] (f) Omitted

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.34 In this Section—] (g) “person causing the risk” has the meaning given to it in the Protection Measures Regulation;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.34 In this Section—] (h) “protected person” has the meaning given to it in the Protection Measures Regulation;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.34 In this Section—] (i) “protection measure” has the meaning given to it in the Protection Measures Regulation;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.34 In this Section—] (j) “Protection Measures Regulation” means Regulation (EU) No 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12th June 2013 on mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters 10 . ## Procedure for applications in this Section

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > Procedure for applications in this Section] 74.35 Subject to the rules in this Section, applications under the Protection Measures Regulation to the County Court or to the High Court must be made in accordance with Part 23. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > Procedure for applications in this Section] Rules 74.36 to 74.45 omitted

## INCOMING PROTECTION MEASURES

## Application for adjustment under Article 11

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > Application for adjustment under Article 11] 74.46 A protected person may apply to the court under Article 11 of the Protection Measures Regulation to adjust the factual elements of an incoming protection measure. ## Notification of the adjustment under Article 11

## 74.47

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.47] (1)  Subject to paragraph (2), Article 11 notice must be given to the person causing the risk by serving it in accordance with Section III of Part 6 and the rules in that Section apply to service of the notice as they apply to any other document to be served. (2) If the person causing the risk resides in a Member State of the European Union other than the United Kingdom or in a country outside the European Union, Article 11 notice must be given by sending it by registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt or other confirmation of delivery or equivalent to the last known place of residence of that person. ## Enforcement of an incoming protection measure

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > Enforcement of an incoming protection measure] 74.48 Part 81 applies to applications in relation to a breach of an incoming protection measure as if the incoming protection measure had been ordered by the County Court. ## Application for refusal of recognition or enforcement under Article 13

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > Application for refusal of recognition or enforcement under Article 13] 74.49 A person causing the risk may apply to the court under Article 13 of the Protection Measures Regulation for refusal of recognition or enforcement of an incoming protection measure. ## Application under Article 14(2)

## 74.50

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.50] (1)  This rule applies where an Article 14 certificate has been issued in a Member State of the European Union other than the United Kingdom or Denmark. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.50] (2) A protected person or person causing the risk may apply to the court to stay, suspend or withdraw the effects of recognition or, where applicable, the enforcement of the protection measure. (3) An application under this rule must include a copy of the Article 14 certificate issued in the other Member State. (4) On an application under this rule, the court must make such orders or give such directions as may be necessary to give effect to the Article 14 certificate. ## Footnotes
